document.title: Helios VEX - Modicon M340 controller (CVE-2019-6819, source not collected)

publisher.name: Helios Industrial Security Lab
publisher.contact_details: Helios Industrial Security Lab, 42 Example Way, Springfield / vex@example.org

revision_history.summary: Source collection failed, so the status stays under_investigation; applied vendor mitigations point to likely_mitigated.

full_product_names.name: Schneider Electric Modicon M340 BMXP342020 Firmware V3.20

full_product_name.name: Embedded Modbus/TCP service module V3.20 as a component of Schneider Electric Modicon M340 BMXP342020 Firmware V3.20

vulnerabilities.title: Improper input validation while handling Modbus requests on Modicon controllers (CWE-20)

notes.title: Vulnerability summary
notes.text: The Modbus/TCP interface does not sufficiently validate certain crafted requests, so an unauthenticated attacker can drive the controller into a denial-of-service state.

notes.title: Basis for the VEX verdict
notes.text: The controller firmware is distributed as binary only, so the source could not be collected (source_code_available=false) and the official status of CSAFPID-0010 is under_investigation. The semantic estimate and its evidence are recorded in analysis.semantic_estimation. Mitigations do not change whether the vulnerable code is present, so the official status is not raised to not_affected.

notes.title: Why the source could not be collected
notes.text: Binary-only firmware; the vendor distributes neither source nor a build recipe for the Modicon runtime.

semantic_estimation.rationale: Every compensating control named in the vendor advisory is confirmed applied on this asset, and the IP allowlist removes the unauthenticated network path the vulnerability depends on, so likely_mitigated leads. likely_affected stays medium rather than low because the vulnerable code is presumed present and the mitigations are configuration state that a change could undo.

evidence.value: application password and Modbus write protection enabled
firmware V3.20 is inside the advisory range

hbom_evidence.relevance: The Modbus/TCP exposure point, though the field configuration has an IP allowlist enabled.
Confirms the model supports the mitigation settings named in the vendor advisory (write protection).

threats.details: Were the impact to hold, the controller would halt and process availability would be lost; the applied access controls sharply narrow the reachable path.
Not listed in CISA KEV, and EPSS 0.00412 indicates low exploitation pressure.

remediations.details: Keep the mitigations currently in place (application password, Modbus write protection, IP allowlist) and re-evaluate whenever the configuration changes.
Updating to the latest vendor firmware applies the underlying fix and removes the dependence on compensating controls.
